name: Shanghai
tagline: The xiaolongbao of Yu Garden against the no-sign spot that competes with crab.

Nanxiang Steamed Bun Restaurant.description: The historic xiaolongbao spot inside Yu Garden, Shanghai's most famous even as it now shares space with tourism.

Jia Jia Tang Bao.description: A tiny spot with a permanent line; its crab xiaolongbao is considered superior to Nanxiang's by many locals.

Di Shui Dong.description: Loud, no-frills Hunanese cooking, famous for its cumin ribs. Anthony Bourdain visited on "Parts Unknown."

Fu He Hui.description: Chinese vegetarian haute cuisine in Changning, among Asia's 50 best restaurants. Two Michelin stars.

Fu 1039.description: Home-style Shanghainese cooking in a 1920s European-style mansion, from chef Tony Lu. One of food writer Fuchsia Dunlop's personal favorites.
